newsitem.title: LEBANON: FOCUS - Beirut Banque Audi H1 profits rise.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Beirut Banque Audi H1 profits rise.

text.p: Lebanon's Banque Audi reported on Wednesday that net profits rose 18.7 percent to 17.02 billion pounds ($11.05 million) in the first half of 1997 over the same period of 1996.
The bank also said its assets grew 31.7 percent during the period to 3,081.24 billion Lebanese pounds, mainly due to a rise in customer deposits.
"This performance has been translated into a net return on average assets (in annualised terms) of 1.15 percent and a return on shareholders equity of 18.38 percent," the bank said in a statement.
The bank said net profits in the first half of 1996 were 14.34 billion Lebanese pounds and profits for the full year stood at 30.71 billion pounds.
One stock market analyst said the profits were in line with forecasts while another banking source termed them "slightly better than expectations."
Bank Audi stock, which started trading at $15 in January, closed on Wednesday at $28.75, unchanged from the record high on Tuesday.

The bank, which listed on the Beirut Stock Exchange (BSE) in January, said its market share in the crowded Lebanese banking sector rose to around 7.66 percent this June from 7.41 percent in June 1996.
The company reported that cost-to-income ratio fell from 63.49 percent to 61.77 percent in the year.

The ratio of provisions for doubtful debts to total loans rose from 2.83 percent in June 1996 to 3.64 percent in June 1997, the company said. The capital adequacy ratio rose to 14.26 percent from 13.21 percent.
Bank Audi in 1996 rated sixth among Lebanon's then existing 82 banks in terms of net profits and third in terms of assets. Many brokers regard it as the 10-share Beirut exchange's blue chip stock.
Bank Audi earlier this month announced it had bought Credit Commercial du Moyen-Orient. The bank said on Wednesday this would add about one percent to its market share.
